newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 19.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.

- Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness, the leaders of the political wing of the Irish Republican Army, Sinn Fein, are to address a special party conference on "conflict resolution" in County Meath this weekend amid conflicting signs about the IRA's intentions.
- Ireland's Minister for Justice, Nora Owen, on Monday received the report of the independent inquiry into how Judge Dominic Lynch was not informed of his removal from the Special Criminal Court.

- Independent Irish airline Ryanair is currently involved in negotiations with banks to fund the acquisition of aircraft for the airline's planned expansion into Europe, chief executive Michael O'Leary said.
- The Irish pound has managed to remain steady against sterling, after the UK currency reached four-year highs against the dollar.

- A special inquiry into the series of blunders that led to the Judge Dominic Lynch affair does not single out a culprit for the mistakes but exposes administrative chaos with the Department of Justice.
- Plans to murder the North's Lord Chief Justice, off-duty prison officers and building contractors have been found by the RUC in a suspected IRA intelligence cell in Belfast.

- Failure to reach agreement on an EMU Stability Pact at next month's EU Summit in Dublin may have serious implications for interest rates in the countries which are expected to be participants in a single currency, according to Eoin Fahy, senior economist with Ulster Bank Markets.
